solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Genre of film associated with boldness in a war zone

parts.note: a western is a film genre of cowboys and the American frontier
front means nerve or cheek, as in 'he had the front to ask'

explanation.surface: A film critic links cowboy movies with courage under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Western Front was the line of trenches across Belgium and France in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Western Front was the main battle line in France and Belgium during the First World War, a theatre of fighting.

clue.text: Stealing floats, they say? Scapegoats found

indicators.note: a phrase reporting speech, signalling that the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: whipping is slang for stealing, and buoys are floats moored at sea

explanation.surface: A question about pinching floats, then a sudden discovery of people to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whipping buoys' (pinching floats) is pronounced the same as the phrase meaning scapegoats; 'they say' signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipping boy was once punished in place of a young prince, so the term now means anyone blamed for others' faults.

clue.text: Celebrity, last in event to jump

parts.note: a star is a famous person

indicators.note: asks for only the final letter of the word event

explanation.surface: A famous person, the final competitor in some contest, is about to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to jump or flinch suddenly in surprise, a verb sense of both words.

clue.text: Stylish member in neat pants

indicators.note: places one piece inside the other
British slang for rubbish or badly done, so the word neat is to be jumbled

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A shapely limb looks chic in a tidy pair of trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers but is British slang for rubbish, so it signals the anagram; 'in' then does the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and elegant are synonyms, both describing graceful, tasteful appearance.

clue.text: Nobleman entering New York? Just about

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other

parts.note: an earl is a British peer

explanation.surface: An aristocrat arriving in America is asked whether he has more or less made it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and just about are synonyms meaning almost but not quite.

clue.text: Noisy mob, heading off before end of rally

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a mob is a crowd of people

indicators.note: asks for the final letter of the word rally

explanation.surface: A loud crowd breaks away before a political rally finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdy describes loud, disorderly behaviour, a close synonym of noisy.

clue.text: English sailor hurried over to tell the story

indicators.note: in a down clue this turns the assembled letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a seaman
ran means hurried

explanation.surface: An English seaman rushed across to recount his tale.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to recount events in order, the act of telling a tale.

clue.text: We lament goal scrambled in college match

indicators.note: something scrambled is mixed up, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Players bemoan a messy goal conceded in a school fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eton wall game is an ancient, famously low-scoring football-like game played at Eton College, the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: The wall game is played annually at Eton College, so it is a match belonging to that college.

clue.text: Picture that is enthralling the old lady, first in guidebook

indicators.note: to enthrall is to hold captive, so one piece holds the others within it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
old lady is slang for mother, so MA

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of guidebook

explanation.surface: A photo that captivates Mum is the leading one in a travel guide.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture, likeness or depiction, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Dodgy two-star, taking the most pessimistic view

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shady hotel with two stars is judged with gloomy expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'at worst' means assuming the bleakest outcome, the most gloomy possible view.

clue.text: Unforeseen difficulty in mine before collapse

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
to fall is to collapse

explanation.surface: A hidden problem in a colliery before a cave-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or snag, originally a concealed hole to trap animals.

clue.text: Long tale about Melibee, ultimately

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a yarn is a long story

indicators.note: means at the end, so only the final letter of Melibee

explanation.surface: A lengthy story about Melibee, from Chaucer's Canterbury Tales, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is the verb (to desire), not the adjective. The Tale of Melibee is one of Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something and to yearn for it are synonyms, both meaning to desire intensely.

clue.text: Declare invalid's wife released from old London gaol

indicators.note: the letter is let out, taken away from the prison's name

parts.note: Newgate was a notorious prison in the City of London, closed in 1902

explanation.surface: An invalid's wife is freed from a historic London prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declare invalid's' reads as a sick person's wife, but the 's is just 'is' linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to nullify or cancel, declaring something void.

clue.text: A lot of blood over area surrounding sick animal

indicators.note: the pieces go around another one
in a down clue the first piece sits above the next
most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Much blood spread over the ground around a sick creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' drops the last letter; 'over' stacks the pieces in this down clue; 'surrounding' wraps them round the sick piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla is a large African ape, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Arrived ahead of artist, producer of pictures

parts.note: came means arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist

explanation.surface: A painter turned up early, a maker of images.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera takes photographs, so it is a device that makes pictures.

clue.text: Plug clothes in speech

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an advertisement or ad
to dress is to clothe

explanation.surface: A speaker promotes a clothing line during a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk delivered to an audience.

clue.text: Carried round island in the Pacific

parts.note: borne is the past participle of bear, to carry
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone is carried around an island in a tropical ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is a large island in South-East Asia, bordered by Pacific seas.

clue.text: Flog wood

definitions.meaning: to beat with a bundle of twigs
the pale timber of the tree

explanation.surface: An instruction to whip some timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Birch is both a tree's timber and, as a verb, to thrash with birch twigs.

clue.text: Hospital teas prepared in great speed

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: the letters are made up into a fresh form, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Cups of tea are made at a hospital in a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is hurry, acting with great speed.

clue.text: Second, perhaps, to have spoken about loud noise

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written
a din is a racket

explanation.surface: A second witness to have spoken about a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second, perhaps' looks like a unit of time; it is an example of a number expressing position.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like first, second and third are ordinal numbers, showing position in a sequence.

clue.text: In Medina, tales of birth

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the run of letters in the next words

explanation.surface: Stories of nativity told in the Arabian holy city of Medina.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is an adjective relating to birth, as in prenatal care.

clue.text: Russian leader travelling in style

indicators.note: something travelling moves about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A Russian president journeys luxuriously.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was the first president of the Russian Federation, 1991 to 1999.

clue.text: Tear off to collect ten more

indicators.note: one piece gathers in the other
something off has gone bad or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Rip something away to gather ten additional items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns TEAR into ETRA; 'to collect' puts X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, more than the usual amount.

clue.text: Produced German wine entertaining one unmarried French girl

parts.note: made means produced

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Moselle is a white wine from the Mosel valley in Germany
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: German wine was served while hosting a single French girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title for a young or single woman, equivalent to Miss.
